definitions.explanation: The traditional Japanese sitting posture of kneeling with legs folded underneath, sitting on one's heels. Considered the most formal way to sit on tatami.

examples.japanese: {正座|せいざ}して{待|ま}っていた。
examples.english: I was waiting in formal sitting position.

examples.japanese: {長|なが}い{時間|じかん}{正座|せいざ}すると{足|あし}が{痺|しび}れる。
examples.english: Your legs go numb if you sit in seiza for a long time.

examples.japanese: {茶道|さどう}では{正座|せいざ}が{基本|きほん}の{姿勢|しせい}とされている。
examples.english: In the tea ceremony, seiza is considered the standard posture.

notes:
KANJI:
{正|せい} (correct/proper) + {座|ざ} (sitting). Literally "correct sitting."

USAGE:
{正座|せいざ}する is the verb form (to sit in seiza). This posture is expected in formal settings like {茶道|さどう} (tea ceremony), {書道|しょどう} (calligraphy), and {武道|ぶどう} (martial arts), as well as at funerals and formal gatherings on {畳|たたみ}.

Many modern Japanese people find {正座|せいざ} uncomfortable for extended periods, and it is common for legs to fall asleep ({足|あし}が{痺|しび}れる).

NOTE ON HOMOPHONES:
Do not confuse with {星座|せいざ} (constellation), which has the same reading.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {正座|せいざ}する: to sit in seiza
- {正座|せいざ}を{崩|くず}す: to shift out of seiza into a more relaxed position
- {足|あし}が{痺|しび}れる: legs go numb (from seiza)
